newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai central bank wants merger for Finance One.
newsitem.headline: Thai central bank wants merger for Finance One.

text.p: Thailand's central bank wants debt-ridden Finance One Plc to enter into fresh merger talks with other parties, a senior official said on Thursday.

Swangchit Chaiyawat, manager of the Bank of Thailand's financial institutions development told Reuters that she understood Finance One was now in talks with another party on a proposed merger. On Wednesday, a government source said the firm was in merger talks with KrungThai Thanakit Finance and Securities.

The bank declined to subscribe to Finance One's rights issue -- which closed for subscription on Wednesday -- because government decrees announced on Tuesday gave the bank more flexibility in handling the firm's situation, Sawangchit said.
"Yesterday was the deadline and we decided not to buy shares because we have a new choice, after the new decrees we will provide the company a new choice of merging with other companies," she said.
The outcome of merger talks was dependent on the willingness of a potential partner for Finance One, she said.

Finance One officials declined to comment on the matter. The firm's plan to merge with Thai Danu Bank Plc collapsed last month with both parties citing tax and legal complications. Some analysts said the failure may also have been due to Finance One's hefty debts.

Krungthai Thanakit, cited as a new potential merging partner, said it would have to compile a study into any possible tie-up. Any transaction involving the company would not damage its operations, the firm said in a statement to the Stock Exchange of Thailand on Thursday.

"The clarification must be made that the BOT has not contacted or made assignment to KTT at all," the statement said. It added that KTT would not conduct any transactions which would cause damage to its operations, its shareholders, or the operations of any other company.
The statement was in response to local media reports which speculated that Krungthai Thanakit has been pressured by the authorities into merging with Finance One.

Once the country's largest non-bank financial institution, Finance One has been hit by the severe downturn in Thailand's economy and is currently in talks with international creditors to reschedule debt payments worth around $46.4 million.
